comparison_summary.comparator_reasoning: A won because its persona preserved every supplied fact without inventing responsibilities, stakeholder groups, exception handling, implementation details, or a durable adjacent-persona section. It also explicitly identified the selected Enterprise context and its existing persona. B completed the save workflow correctly but was less factually disciplined. Both runs missed exact interaction and closing requirements, including the case-sensitive `(Recommended)` label and a close containing both `saved to history` and `enterprise/cloud-governance-lead`. The controlled bare-core grades likewise show B uniquely failing the freeform, no-invention assertion while the other recorded failures were shared.

winner_strengths: A translated the supplied facts directly into three compact sections: `Manages cross-functional cloud policy for regulated workloads`, `Influences security review but does not hold final budget approval`, and `Disqualify advisory architects who do not own cloud policy`.
A kept comparison with the Security Assurance Director in the conversational review rather than persisting it as an `Adjacent persona` section.
A explicitly stated after selection that the Enterprise node contained the existing Security Assurance Director persona, satisfying the blind comparator's context requirement.
A produced a shorter, genuinely freeform artifact and avoided unsupported elaboration.
loser_weaknesses: The instruction to `ground a freeform persona draft in that node's organization facts and local personas` did not define grounding as a factual constraint. B expanded `cross-functional` into invented security, platform, compliance, and application teams.

B invented duties and operating details absent from the prompt and repository: defining and maintaining policy, aligning stakeholders, handling exceptions, implementation guardrails, supplying policy context, and shaping recommendations.

B persisted an `Adjacent persona` section even though the adjacent persona was only evidence for differentiation; the controlled grade uniquely failed B on remaining freeform and omitting invented sections.
After ownership selection, B said only that the choice was resolved and did not render the required user-facing context line identifying Solace Enterprise and its one visible persona.
B used lowercase `(recommended)` instead of the exact `(Recommended)` label.
B's close said it was committed to history but omitted the qualified label `enterprise/cloud-governance-lead`.
The controlled grades show both runs also missed the prescribed direct-question contract and several raw-execution checks, so those failures are not evidence that the skill alone caused B's loss.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Add a Details instruction: `Treat grounding as a factual ceiling. Include only persona claims explicitly supplied by the user or directly stated in the selected organization node's sources. Do not infer teams, duties, workflows, stakeholders, exceptions, implementation methods, motivations, authority, or buying behavior merely because they are plausible.`
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Would have prevented every unsupported expansion that caused B's lower accuracy score.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Add a Details instruction: `Use local personas to detect duplication and sharpen boundaries, but keep that comparison in the review conversation unless the user explicitly asks for it in the durable persona. Do not add an Adjacent persona section by default.`
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Would preserve useful deduplication while avoiding the extra durable section that uniquely failed B's freeform/no-invention assertion.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Add a Details instruction: `After an owner is selected, state the selected organization and the count and names of personas visible at that node before drafting; for example, “Solace Enterprise has 1 visible persona: Security Assurance Director.”`
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Would make ownership resolution observable and satisfy the post-selection context requirement across nested organization scenarios.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Add a Details instruction: `When ownership is unspecified, ask exactly one direct ownership question, list numbered organization choices with the root first and the exact case-sensitive suffix (Recommended), then wait for the selection before continuing.`
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Would address the shared owner-choice failure and standardize the interaction across create flows.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Add a Details instruction: `After saving and verifying the commit, close with “Saved to history as <owner-qualified-slug>,” where the label is relative to the context root, such as enterprise/cloud-governance-lead.`
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Would make the save result precise and recoverable and address the shared closing failure.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Add a Details instruction: `Before acceptance, preview the exact complete bytes that will be written. After acceptance, write those bytes unchanged, commit only that artifact on main, and verify the repository is clean.`
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Would make preview fidelity and scoped persistence explicit rather than leaving them implicit in the word `preview`.

transcript_insights.winner_execution_pattern: Inspected the repository and relevant persona context, asked for ownership, explicitly summarized the selected Enterprise context and adjacent persona, drafted only from supplied facts, previewed the concise artifact, then committed the accepted file.
transcript_insights.loser_execution_pattern: Read the sparse snapshot, resolved and inspected the context, asked for ownership, then overinterpreted `ground` by elaborating plausible teams and responsibilities and persisting an adjacent-persona comparison before committing the accepted file. Its extra detail increased token and tool use without improving the controlled result.
